work.agent_query: Read README.md. You are the Medicare Advantage retention-analytics desk as of 2026-01-31. Write strategy/policy.py: allocate(universe, asof) -> {entity_id: weight}, spreading a FINITE retention budget across the 830 eligible MA/Part-D contracts using the boundary feature table (recent enrollment-growth windows, the Jan AEP-month jump, trend/volatility, size, contract age, Part-D flag, MA share, org/plan type). The judge runs your policy once and grades how much of the contracts' ACTUALLY REALIZED Feb->Jun-2026 member loss your budget sat in front of (a hidden future window), on three lanes: coverage hit rate vs the universe median, worst-decile shrinkage tail capture, and loss captured vs the equal-weight benchmark. The budget TARGETS the loss tail (more captured is better). The starter IS the equal-weight budget and scores exactly 0.00. Copying last window's decline ranking is weak (rank persistence is only +0.45 and far weaker on loss magnitude -- post-AEP churn reshuffles who is at risk), and allocating to the largest contracts captures LESS loss than the benchmark -- measured, not hypothetical. Per-contract weight is capped at 0.0120481928 (= 1/83), so a legal book holds at least 83 names. Also write strategy/book_report.json describing the book you submit: the judge recomputes every statistic from your weights and ZEROES your score if you misreport. Offline; policy.py passes a static ALLOWLIST gate -- only pure stdlib maths modules and cms_scorer import; no filesystem, no os/json/csv/numpy/random/time, no open/eval/exec/getattr. Rehearse book shape with `python3 check.py`; it cannot preview your grade (the graded window is hidden by construction).
